The search found little Enable Banking-specific guidance on adding a second redirect URL or an HTTPS rule. The most relevant Enable Banking material is about activation and redirect matching.

**Enable Banking specifics:**
- **Activation:** Enable Banking's own docs say a new production app starts as "Inactive" and becomes active once you link one of your own accounts through the Control Panel. That puts it in restricted mode, where you can only fetch data from accounts linked to the app, until an agreement is signed. Your newly created applications status will be "Inactive". To activate it, connect an account using the "Activate by linking accounts" button After confirming an account link, the application will become active in restricted mode. Using restricted applications you can only fetch data from accounts linked to the application. The application will stay in this state until an agreement has been signed.
- **Redirect URL matching:** A third-party community setup guide says the redirect URL registered with Enable Banking must match the one the app sends, exactly. It warns that mismatches in trailing slash, http versus https, or port cause the bank to refuse the handover. The bank refuses the handover — the redirect URL registered with Enable Banking does not match the one the dashboard sent, exactly. Check for a trailing slash, http against https, and the port. That guide is not official documentation.

**Other providers (not Enable Banking, so treat as context only):**
- Mastercard Open Banking Connect says most ASPSPs will support the addition of multiple redirect urls, but some banks will only support the addition of one redirect url per TPP. It also says that changing a production redirect URL will require a new registration with the bank before it can be used.
- Yapily notes that the Open Banking Directory only supports redirect URLs that use the http and https schemes.

**Gap:** I did not find an Enable Banking page that states whether a production app can hold more than one redirect URL, or whether HTTPS is mandatory. Check the Enable Banking API docs or their support team directly for those two points.

Nothing changes for anyone who leaves this off.

1. In Settings, a new **Phone and tablet** card shows one line and a **Turn on** button.

The phone works like the laptop for pages, chat, voice, imports and sync. The laptop keeps using `localhost`, so its sign-ins work exactly as they do today.

| Service | From the phone | Extra step |
|---|---|---|
| **Banks** | Same as on the laptop | Once only: paste your phone address into your Enable Banking app. Moneo shows it with a copy button |
| **Scalable** | Log in on the phone, then finish with a paste | Each time you connect |

content.text:
**Your idea is how it will work: the phone is just another screen on the Moneo running on your laptop.** My last message made it sound more separate than it is, because the paste step only ever applied to first-time logins.

## What happens when you use the phone
```
Phone or iPad ──> Moneo on your laptop ──> ChatGPT, Scalable, banks, your database
   (screen)         (does all the work)
```
- **Asking ChatGPT something:** the question goes to your laptop, which uses its existing sign-in and sends back the answer. You don't sign in on the phone.
- **Scalable and banks:** you see the same data, and pressing Sync on the phone runs the sync on the laptop with the connection it already has.
- **Changes and edits:** these save to the same database, so they're there on both devices. An already open page can take up to 30 seconds or a refresh to show them. I haven't checked whether a chat reply streams live on both screens at once, like T3 Code does. It may only appear on the other screen once it's saved.

## I'd drop the paste step
Your approach makes it unnecessary, and the plan gets simpler:
- **No paste box:** ChatGPT, Scalable and banks are connected once on the laptop, and the phone uses those connections.
- **No Enable Banking step:** you won't need to add a second return address, which also removes the question I couldn't confirm.

The one case left is a login expiring, or a first connection when you're away from the laptop. The login itself has to happen in the laptop's browser, because ChatGPT and Scalable won't return to any other device. So the phone would show "Reconnect this on your laptop" for that one action, and everything else works normally. Banks can also ask for this, as their consent expires periodically.

## Why the phone still needs Tailscale
Your phone needs a way to reach your laptop over the internet, because Moneo only listens on the laptop. Tailscale doesn't run Moneo or hold your data; it's only that private connection. There are only two realistic ways to do this:

| | Private Tailscale | Public link with a password (Funnel) |
|---|---|---|
| **On the phone** | Install the app once | Nothing, just open the link |
| **On the laptop** | Tailscale, switched on from Settings | Tailscale, switched on from Settings |
| **Getting in** | Your devices go straight in | You enter a password |
| **Who can reach it** | Only your devices | Anyone can reach the login page |
| **Work for me** | Small | I also have to build the login |

The experience of using Moneo is the same either way. T3 Code feels simpler because you just open a link, and Funnel is the closest match to that. I'd still pick private Tailscale for financial data, but this is your call.

## Two questions
1. Are you happy to drop the paste step and show "Reconnect this on your laptop" in that rare case?
2. Private Tailscale, or a public link with a password?

content.content:
**Behavior when logged out or not logged in:** By default, Tailscale on Windows runs within the user's login session. If you sign out or restart, it disconnects until someone logs in again. Unattended mode (also called Server mode) keeps the device reachable in these cases, such as for Remote Desktop access after a reboot.

**Enabling Run Unattended:**
- **Tray UI:** Right-click the Tailscale tray icon, hover over **Preferences**, select **Run unattended**, and confirm **Yes** when prompted.
- **CLI:** Run `tailscale set --unattended=true` in PowerShell or Command Prompt.
- **Enterprise policy:** Set the `UnattendedMode` registry value under `HKLM\Software\Policies\Tailscale` to `always`, `never`, or `user-decides`.

The Windows account that enables unattended mode owns the Tailscale configuration on that device.

**Relevance to sleep:** The article doesn't address sleep or hibernation. It covers only signing out and restarting, so I can't say from this content whether unattended mode affects connectivity during sleep.

content.content:
**Behavior when logged out or not logged in:** By default, Tailscale on Windows runs within the user's login session. If you sign out or restart, it disconnects until someone logs in again. Unattended mode (also called Server mode) keeps the device reachable in these cases, such as for Remote Desktop access after a reboot.

**Enabling Run Unattended:**
- **Tray UI:** Right-click the Tailscale tray icon, hover over **Preferences**, select **Run unattended**, and confirm **Yes** when prompted.
- **CLI:** Run `tailscale set --unattended=true` in PowerShell or Command Prompt.
- **Enterprise policy:** Set the `UnattendedMode` registry value under `HKLM\Software\Policies\Tailscale` to `always`, `never`, or `user-decides`.

The Windows account that enables unattended mode owns the Tailscale configuration on that device.

**Relevance to sleep:** The article doesn't address sleep or hibernation. It covers only signing out and restarting, so I can't say from this content whether unattended mode affects connectivity during sleep.

**HTTPS not enabled:** For an HTTPS serve (the default), the CLI calls `enableFeatureInteractive(ctx, "serve", nodecap.HTTPS)`. If that fails, it returns `error enabling https feature: <cause>`. The function body isn't included, so I can't tell what prompt or URL it shows. A `--bg` serve returns right after setting config. Only foreground mode waits, looping on the IPN bus until interrupted.

**Success output:** The CLI prints either "Available within your tailnet:" or "Available on the internet:" (Funnel), followed by the URL. For background serves it adds:
- `"%s started and running in the background."`, e.g. "Serve started and running in the background."
- A disable hint: "To disable the proxy, run: tailscale %s --%s=%d off"

Foreground mode ends with "Press Ctrl+C to exit."

**Port already in use:** Errors are printed as `error: <cause>` followed by a pointer to `--help`:
- Web over TCP: "cannot serve web; already serving TCP"
- TCP over web: "cannot serve TCP; already serving web on %d for %s"

The `--yes` flag only skips the confirmation prompt when removing multiple handlers under a port: "Are you sure you want to delete %d handlers under port %s?" The source shows no prompt for overwriting an existing handler, and `SetWebHandler` isn't included, so I can't confirm overwrite behavior.

**Turning off:** Append `off` as the final argument, for example `tailscale serve --https=443 off`. That calls `unsetServe`, which removes the web handler, TCP forwarding, or TUN config for that port. If the handler doesn't exist, it returns "handler does not exist." `tailscale serve reset` also exists as a subcommand.

**Status JSON:** Yes. `tailscale serve status` accepts `--json`, described as "output JSON." The same applies to `funnel status`.

**The plan has no blockers, but one practical problem:** this PC is a laptop, so when it sleeps, Moneo is unreachable from your phone. The rest are smaller items that the steps below handle or you can accept.

## What I checked
- **Connection:** Tailscale's source code shows it passes the original address through to Moneo, so form actions shouldn't get blocked.
- **Reachability:** the browser only talks to Moneo directly, apart from chat attachments, which step 1 fixes.
- **Phone locking mid-chat:** the reply keeps running on the laptop, because the chat code is written to survive this.
- **Sign-ins:** only three places start a login (bank, Scalable, ChatGPT), and the laptop's addresses for them don't change.

## Problems to know about
1. **Sleep and restarts (the main one):** Moneo can't fix this from inside the app.
   - **Sleep:** keep the laptop plugged in and set closing the lid to "Do nothing".
   - **Restarts:** Docker and Moneo have to start again, and Tailscale needs `tailscale set --unattended=true` to stay connected after a restart. I'd add auto-start to `BACKLOG.md` as later work.
2. **No live mirroring like T3 Code:** the data is shared, but I found no code that pushes a chat to other open screens as it happens. A question asked on the phone runs and saves, and the laptop shows it once you reopen or refresh that chat. I'd leave this for later too, since it's a separate feature.
3. **Your laptop's name becomes public:** turning on HTTPS publishes the address in certificate logs, and this PC is named `indkhan`. No financial data is exposed, but rename the machine in the Tailscale admin console first.
4. **A lost phone has full access:** keep a screen lock on, and remove the device in Tailscale if it goes missing.
5. **Voice:** it still needs an OpenAI API key, same as on the laptop. A ChatGPT plan alone won't cover it.
6. **Testing limit:** Tailscale isn't installed here, so I can only test the switch against a simulated Tailscale. The real test needs you.

## Implementation steps
Each step gets its own commit:

1. **Attachments:** send chat files through Moneo instead of Supabase, starting with a failing test.
2. **Safety check:** have Moneo refuse requests that arrive through Tailscale Funnel, so no one reaches the automatic sign-in if Funnel gets turned on by accident.
3. **Tailscale control (`lib/phone-access.ts`):** find Tailscale, read its status, and turn serving on or off. It won't overwrite another app already using that port.
4. **Settings card:** add **Phone and tablet**, off by default, with one line and a **Turn on** button.
   - **While setting up:** it only shows the step you're missing: install, sign in, or approve HTTPS.
   - **Once on:** it shows the address, a QR code to scan, and the phone steps. The QR code adds one small dependency, but saves typing a long address on a phone.
5. **Reconnect message:** if a bank, Scalable or ChatGPT login is started from the phone, it shows "Reconnect this on your laptop" and starts nothing. Sync, disconnect and everything else work as normal.
6. **Small fixes:** remove the portrait lock so tablets can rotate, and allow `*.ts.net` in `npm run dev`.
7. **Docs:** update `README.md` with setup and keeping the laptop awake, update the `AGENTS.md` rule you approved and its callback section, and add auto-start and live mirroring to `BACKLOG.md`.
8. **My testing:** run unit tests, lint and a build, plus a browser test through a simulated Tailscale connection using the QA user, not your data.

## Then you test it with me
1. Install Tailscale on the laptop, phone and iPad, and rename the laptop.
2. Press **Turn on** in Settings and scan the QR code.
3. We check pages, chat, a sync, an attachment, a voice call and the reconnect message on the real devices, then lock the phone mid-chat and check the reply is there afterwards.

Should I start on step 1?

## Setup

1. Start the backend: `npm run setup`.
2. Create the QA user and save its session: `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs`. Its login is stored in `.env` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, and its session in `e2e/.auth.json` (or set `E2E_STORAGE_STATE`).
3. Before a full run, empty its workspace: `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs --reset`. Never delete the user.

Tests never use the owner's workspace: a saved QA session takes the place of the owner's automatic sign-in.

## Running

```sh
npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1
```

Use one worker: several specs change the same QA workspace and its preferences. Stop a running server on port 3000 before `npm run build`, so the two don't write `.next` at the same time.

## Kinds of specs

- `*.smoke.spec.ts` and `*.mocked.spec.ts` need no saved session; mocked specs stub API responses to check UI contracts.
- `*.gated.spec.ts` need the backend. Most use the QA session; others create disposable users with the service key, sign them in by session cookie, and remove them in `finally`. If interrupted, their IDs are left in ignored `.qa/` files for cleanup.
- `core-journey.gated.spec.ts` calls the real AI provider, so it costs money: run it only when you mean to.
- `review-runtime.config.ts` and `review-investigation.config.ts` run the real Workflow engine against local synthetic database and model servers (ports 3040/3041), including a server restart mid-review: `npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts`.

A skipped spec is not a pass: it means a prerequisite (backend, QA session, service key) is missing.

## Acceptance

`npm run acceptance:fast` runs unit tests, lint and the build. `npm run acceptance:required` then runs the SQL regressions, live database checks and the browser suite on that build with one worker. Results go to an ignored `.qa/acceptance-*` folder; logs there may contain workspace data, so keep them out of the repo.

## Scalable

`scalable-trading.gated.spec.ts` drives chat against a local stand-in for Scalable's MCP server (`e2e/mocks/scalable-mcp.mjs`, made-up data) with the real AI model. Start the app with `SCALABLE_MCP_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3043` and run the spec with the same variable; the spec starts the stand-in, adds a Scalable connection to the QA workspace and removes it afterwards. It checks that an order is previewed on a card and sent only when the card is tapped, once, and that read-only access is told it can't trade.
import { defineConfig, devices } from "@playwright/test";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";

if (existsSync(".env")) process.loadEnvFile(".env");
const production = process.env.E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD === "1";
// E2E_BASE_URL points the suite at an app that is already running (for example a production build on another port).
const external = process.env.E2E_BASE_URL;

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./e2e",
  // e2e/*.test.ts are Vitest unit tests, not browser specs.
  testMatch: "**/*.spec.ts",
  use: {
    baseURL: external ?? "http://localhost:3000",
  },
  webServer: external ? undefined : {
    command: production ? "npm start" : "npm run dev",
    port: 3000,
    reuseExistingServer: !production && !process.env.CI,
  },
  projects: [{ name: "chromium", use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"] } }],
});

content.thinking:
I'm confident the desktop build won't get slower: the status check only runs on the Settings page, inside Suspense so it doesn't block that page, and a missing CLI fails fast via an existence check. The proxy only does a single header check, and there's no scheduler to worry about.

Next I'm drafting the attachments step, where the test should confirm that GET returns the file bytes with the right content type, never redirects, and sends the nosniff header. I'm starting on the download call from the chat storage bucket.

Next I'm working out the response shape for the attachment download, weighing whether the content type should come from storage or be derived from the file extension, since uploads were only sniffed for jpeg, png, webp, and pdf. I'm also considering whether a sandbox CSP would break inline PDF viewing, and leaning toward nosniff alone.

I'm sketching the phone-access module now: a CLI lookup that tries known install paths and then the PATH, a status check that treats a non-Running backend state as signed out, and a fallback to the same signed-out state if the local service isn't reachable at all.

I'm working through the phone-access setup now: the server should use the Serve status to check that the public HTTPS port on the machine points at the local app and not something else, and if it's pointed at something else, I'll report it as busy. The app port comes from the environment with 3000 as the default, so I'll set the proxy target to the local address on that port and verify the actual behavior afterward.

I'm working out the sign-in step: the user has to log in to their Tailscale account themselves, since I can't do that for them, so I'll get the login URL from the CLI and have them complete it in the browser before I go on.

I'm weighing how to make the sign-in step work: the simplest route is to run `tailscale login` and capture the login URL it prints, then show the user a link to finish signing in in their browser.

I'm checking how the enable flow should behave: if the machine is signed out, I'll capture the login link from the CLI, and if it's off, I'll turn serving on and then look for an approval link. Before relying on the login-capture approach, I want to test what `tailscale login` prints and whether its URL still works after the process is killed.

I'm weighing whether the unattended setting should be turned on for Windows so the phone link survives a reboot, but changing that without the owner's say seems wrong, so I'll leave it to them to decide.

I'm deciding where the phone-request check should live: a small helper that reads the forwarded host or host header and tests for a .ts.net suffix, kept free of the child-process code so the routes can import it. Then the bank connect path needs a request argument, and the ChatGPT action will redirect with a message in the query string.

I'm now checking the bank and Scalable reconnect paths, since they both go through the same connect route, so the new request check will cover them too. I'll show a short note that bank logins have to start on the computer running Moneo, and I'll test the route with a forwarded host header.

I'm now weighing how to show the phone-access card: a QR code rendered on the server, which keeps the dependency out of the client bundle, and only when the link is on.

I'm settling on a Color choice for the QR code: a white background so it scans in dark mode too. Next I'm checking the uqr package's version and age before installing it, then I'll build the server component that wraps the phone-access status in Suspense, with actions for turning access on and off that route the QR rendering through the server.

I'm settling the phone-access card's copy for each state, starting with the off state: a short line saying the feature is optional and changes nothing until it's turned on, plus a Turn on button. The not-installed case will only show after the button is pressed, so the client needs to track whether it's been clicked.

I'm settling the initial view for the phone-access card: the page only shows the on state up front, and any busy, missing, or signed-out result appears only after the user presses the button. Next I'm drafting the not-installed copy, with a link to the Tailscale download page and a line saying only the user's own signed-in devices can reach Moneo, plus a Check again button.

I'm settling the phone-access card's error handling: if an action fails, the card falls back to the off state and shows the error. The on state will show the QR code and address alongside three setup steps and a note to keep the computer awake, with a Turn off button that asks for confirmation first, since turning it off cuts off any connected phone.

I'm going to check whether the command palette has any settings deep-links, then look at the next.config allowed origins, since a single-label wildcard won't cover a two-label tailnet hostname. I'll also write up the README and agent rules and the callback notes, and test how the Tailscale login behaves before building on it.

OPEN
Open Moneo on your phone from any network, with nothing to install on the phone. Moneo only listens on 127.0.0.1 today, and it signs its owner in automatically, so any remote access must add a login first (an `APP_PASSWORD` sign-in, or Cloudflare Access).

- Options weighed: Tailscale Funnel (free, fixed `*.ts.net` URL, nothing on the phone), Cloudflare Tunnel (free tunnel; a fixed URL needs your own domain, about $10/yr), or Tailscale with its phone app (private, no password needed).
- HTTPS is required for voice: browsers only give web pages the microphone over a secure connection.
- Bank connections from the phone: register the tunnel's `https://…/api/bank/callback` as a second redirect URL in Enable Banking, and send the bank back to whichever address the owner started from (laptop: `https://localhost:3443`).
- Callbacks: ChatGPT sign-in only accepts a 127.0.0.1 callback and Scalable's login accepts localhost freely, so both are connected from the computer Moneo runs on; their syncs then work from anywhere.

**Phone and tablet access is built and works through your real Tailscale address, and it's ready for you to try on your actual phone and tablet.** It's on the local branch `t3/mobile-access-options`, not pushed or merged yet.

## Tested through your real `ts.net` address
I used the QA test user in a phone-sized browser on the laptop, not your data.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Settings switch** | Starts off and shows one line and a button; turning it on and off works |
| **Pages** | Home, accounts, plan, import and settings all loaded in 0.2–0.7 seconds |
| **Form actions** | Work through Tailscale |
| **Chat attachments** | Upload and open correctly |
| **Live replies** | Arrived line by line with almost no delay, tested with a small stand-in stream |
| **Voice requirement** | The browser reports a secure page with the microphone available |
| **Logins from a phone** | ChatGPT, bank and Scalable show the "use the computer" message and start nothing |
| **No session** | Refused (401) |

Unit tests (1408 passed, 10 skipped), lint and build all pass. I didn't run the full Playwright browser suite, only my test of this flow.

## For people who don't turn it on
- **Tailscale:** Moneo doesn't start or need Tailscale, except for one quick status check on the Settings page. That took about 100 ms and doesn't hold up the rest of the page.
- **Other pages:** they only gain one quick header check, and the new QR code library isn't sent to the browser. I didn't run a separate before-and-after speed test.
- **Laptop sign-ins:** the laptop's addresses for ChatGPT, banks and Scalable haven't changed.

## Still only testable on your devices
- A home-screen install on iOS and Android.
- A real voice call, and a real chat reply. The test server had no AI key.
- The phone locking mid-chat. The chat code is built to finish the reply, but I haven't tried it.

## What you need to do
1. **Replace your Enable Banking key**, since my command printed it into this conversation.
2. **Get this code onto your main copy.** Your main copy doesn't have it yet, so tell me to merge it or open a pull request. Phone access is off until then, and I removed the test server and its settings.
3. **On the laptop, after merging,** run this from your main copy, then go to **Settings → Keys and connections → Phone and tablet** and press **Turn on**:
   ```sh
   npm ci
   npm run setup
   npm run build
   npm start
   ```
4. **On your phone and tablet,** install Tailscale, sign in with the same account, scan the QR code, and choose Add to Home Screen.

## Also changed
- **On your laptop:** Tailscale is installed and signed in, and I started Docker Desktop, which is still running.
- **`AGENTS.md`:** it now allows private Tailscale access without a login, while anything public still needs one.
- **New dependency:** I added `uqr` for the QR code.
- **GitHub:** I opened [#165: auto-start after a restart](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/issues/165) and [#166: live chat on every open screen](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/issues/166), and added the new plan to [#157](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/issues/157).

### Findings

**1. REAL PROBLEM (high): artifact charts break on the phone.** This breaks requirement 1.
- **Where:** `app/ai/artifacts/[id]/frame/route.ts:35`, used by `lib/ai/artifact-data.ts:187` and `:233`.
- **Cause:** `new URL(request.url).origin` does not follow the forwarded host. With `Host` and `X-Forwarded-Host` set to `pc.example.ts.net` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, this Next version gave `request.url = https://localhost:3987/u`.
- **Failure:** the page's CSP and the rewritten ECharts script both point at `https://localhost:3000/artifact-lib/...`. On the phone, that is the phone itself. Any ECharts artifact, including Home cards using this frame, shows no chart. It should then show "Part of this page failed to run", which blames the page and suggests asking chat to fix it.
- **Fix:** build the origin from `x-forwarded-proto` and `x-forwarded-host` when `fromRemoteDevice` is true, and add a route test. The laptop keeps its current path. Then test a chart on a real phone.

**2. REAL PROBLEM (medium): "Only devices signed in to your Tailscale account" is false on a shared tailnet.**
- **Where:** `app/settings/phone-access-card.tsx:25`, `proxy.ts:11-27`.
- **Failure:** on a work or family tailnet, any member whose ACLs allow it who opens the address is signed in automatically and gets the full finance app, including trades and Disconnect. The README warns about this, but the card does not, and the card is what people read.
- **Fix:** at minimum, correct the card copy. Better, have `proxy.ts` compare the `Tailscale-User-Login` header that Serve adds with the laptop owner's login, and refuse anyone else. I confirmed the Funnel header string is in `tailscaled.exe`. The `Tailscale-User-Login` behaviour is from my knowledge of Tailscale, not tested.

**3. REAL PROBLEM (medium): the Funnel guard misses the workflow endpoints, and the card ignores Funnel.**
- **Where:** `proxy.ts:30` (matcher), `lib/phone-access.ts:20-24`.
- **Gap:** `.well-known/workflow/` skips the proxy, so the 403 never runs there. The local-world queue handler (`world-local/dist/queue.js:267`) only checks that its `x-vqs-*` headers parse, with no auth I could find in that handler. With Funnel on, the internet can POST to these routes.
- **Could not verify:** whether this is exploitable, since it likely needs a valid run ID.
- **Other paths are fine:** paths ending in `.png` or similar also skip the proxy, but they skip auto sign-in too, so `requireWorkspace` still returns 401. `_next/static` and `artifact-lib` are public by design.
- **Misleading card:** if the owner enables Funnel, the card still says "On. Only devices signed in…", because `serveSchema` ignores `AllowFunnel`.
- **Fix:** add a matcher entry for `/.well-known/workflow/:path*` with `has: [{ type: "header", key: "tailscale-funnel-request" }]`. Also parse `AllowFunnel` and show a warning on the card.

**4. REAL PROBLEM (medium): after a restart the phone hits a dead end, and the card doesn't warn about it.**
- **Where:** `app/settings/phone-access-card.tsx:25`, `README.md:125`.
- **Failure:** the Tailscale forward persists, but Moneo and Docker don't auto-start (`npm start` is manual). The phone should get a bare proxy error (exact page not checked) with no next step. The card says the computer must be "on and awake" but not that Moneo must be running.
- **README gap:** it gives the Tailscale `--unattended` tip but no restart instructions. It says Moneo must be running, not that `npm start` and Docker are needed again after a restart.
- **Fix:** add a line to the card and the README: "After a restart, start Moneo again on this computer (`npm start`)."

**5. REAL PROBLEM (medium): the card says "off" when Tailscale is merely down.**
- **Where:** `app/settings/phone-access.tsx:7`, `lib/phone-access.ts:53-58`.
- **Failure:** the page turns every state except `on` into `off`. After a restart, or with Tailscale stopped, the forward is still saved but the card shows "Nothing changes unless you turn this on" and a Turn on button. The owner can believe access is off, and it comes back when Tailscale reconnects.
- **Side effects:** a `Stopped` backend is treated as `signed_out`, so pressing the button runs `tailscale login` and the copy says "sign in" when the user only needs to connect. I did not run `login`, so its effect on a stopped node is unverified. Turn off is also a silent no-op in this state.
- **Fix:** add a distinct "Tailscale isn't connected" state, shown only if a forward can be read or the owner has asked. Use `tailscale up`-style wording for `Stopped` rather than sign-in.

**6. REAL PROBLEM (low-medium): the "busy" state falsely blames another app and gives no way out.**
- **Where:** `lib/phone-access.ts:47-49`, `phone-access-card.tsx:15`.
- **Failure:** if Moneo's `PORT` changes, or the machine or tailnet is renamed, Moneo's own old forward reads as "Another app… turn that off first". The UI does not say how, and Moneo won't touch it.
- **Fix:** name the current target, and give the command: `tailscale serve --https=443 off`.

**7. REAL PROBLEM (low-medium): actionable CLI errors are hidden from the user.**
- **Where:** `app/settings/phone-access-actions.ts:12-15`.
- **Failure:** on Linux, `tailscale serve` as a non-root user typically fails with an "Access denied… set --operator" message (from memory, not run here). The user only sees "Open Tailscale, check it is connected", which is wrong for that case and a dead end. The real text goes to the server log only.
- **Fix:** detect "Access denied", or show the CLI's first line. Otherwise state in the README that this is unsupported or needs the operator step.

**8. NITPICK: link detection can truncate JSON.** `lib/phone-access.ts:33-36` kills the child on any login URL, including while reading `status --json`, whose `AuthURL` field contains one. If the JSON spans chunks, `JSON.parse` throws: the page shows "off" and the action shows the generic error. A chunk could also cut the URL itself. Only apply the early exit to `login` and `serve`.

**9. NITPICK: mixed streams.** stdout and stderr are combined, so any stderr warning before the JSON turns a healthy Tailscale into `signed_out` (line 41). Parse stdout only.

**10. NITPICK: "removes only Moneo's forward" overstates it.** `serve --https=443 off` should remove all of 443 (from Serve's documented behaviour, not run), so a `/foo` mount added alongside `/` would go too (`lib/phone-access.ts:66`).

**11. NITPICK: copy.**
- `connectOnComputer` says "Open Moneo there" but gives no address.
- The same message appears if the owner opens the `ts.net` link on the laptop itself, which the card invites them to do. That is the only `fromRemoteDevice` misfire I found. `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are unaffected, and `notts.net` is rejected.
- "Those devices lose Moneo" reads oddly when turning off from the phone itself.
- "Add to Home Screen" doesn't say where to find it.
- A bank user on the phone picks a country and bank before being refused.

**Could not verify:**
- **Turning off from the phone:** the action removes the proxy carrying its own response. If the connection drops, the action rejects and may land on the error boundary. Test this live, and catch the failure if it happens.
- **Bank sync from the phone:** `psuFrom` will send a tailnet `100.x` address as the PSU IP (`lib/bank/server.ts:26`). Laptop sync sends a loopback address, so this is probably fine. I did not make real bank calls.

- **Other login routes:** only the bank connect route, Scalable connect route and `startSignIn` start external logins, and all three are guarded. Every connect and reconnect button uses them. 409 errors reach `setError` in the UI, and the ChatGPT message displays. The `request.url` redirects are in callbacks, which only ever run on the laptop.
- **Laptop flows (requirement 3):** the guards are no-ops on `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`, and redirect URIs are unchanged.
- **Non-users (requirement 2):**
  - The card is inside `Suspense`, so a hung CLI can't block Settings; at worst the skeleton waits about 30 seconds.
  - A missing CLI returns quickly via ENOENT, and the card shows one line and a button.
  - The only cost is up to two subprocesses per Settings render.
  - Removing the portrait lock is harmless.
- **CLI handling:** the timeout works, a double resolve is harmless, and malformed JSON or a failing `serve status` is caught on both the page and action paths. Real `serve status --json` output is `{}`, and non-3000 ports follow `PORT` (Next sets it).
- **Attachments:**
  - Access control is intact: the path regex, workspace prefix and RLS client are all still used.
  - Types are limited to jpg/png/webp/pdf, checked by sniffing on upload, so serving them same-origin creates no script risk.
  - The `!` on the type lookup is safe given the regex, and `nosniff` plus `no-store` are set.
  - Files are at most 4 MB, so buffering is fine.
- **Server actions:** both call `requireWorkspace`, and the client-sent `previous` only reaches that same client. CSRF origin checks should pass with the host forwarded.
- **`next.config`:** `**.ts.net` is correct per the Next docs and `csrf-protection.js`, and it only applies in dev.
- **Docs and tailscale flags:** `--unattended` exists (Windows-only, and it covers GUI logout). The ChatGPT guard and the README and app-guide updates are consistent.

2. **No Tailscale:** Turn on leads to an install link and Check again. Fine.
3. **Signed out:** a sign-in link and Check again. Fine, apart from the `Stopped` wording (finding 5).
4. **HTTPS unapproved:** an approval link and Check again. Clear.

`origin/main` has not moved (0 commits behind, 8 ahead).

**Tests (C):** the requested vitest paths passed, 7 files and 24 tests. None of them covers the top finding. No Playwright spec was added for this flow, although AGENTS.md asks for one on changed user flows.

**Not tested live:** I did not run `tailscale serve`, as instructed, and `serve status` on this machine returns `{}`. Header behaviour was checked with a throwaway Next app in the scratchpad (production build, `-H 127.0.0.1`) using simulated forwarded headers.

### Findings

**1. REAL PROBLEM (high): artifact charts break on the phone.** This breaks requirement 1.
- **Where:** `app/ai/artifacts/[id]/frame/route.ts:35`, used by `lib/ai/artifact-data.ts:187` and `:233`.
- **Cause:** `new URL(request.url).origin` does not follow the forwarded host. With `Host` and `X-Forwarded-Host` set to `pc.example.ts.net` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, this Next version gave `request.url = https://localhost:3987/u`.
- **Failure:** the page's CSP and the rewritten ECharts script both point at `https://localhost:3000/artifact-lib/...`. On the phone, that is the phone itself. Any ECharts artifact, including Home cards using this frame, shows no chart. It should then show "Part of this page failed to run", which blames the page and suggests asking chat to fix it.
- **Fix:** build the origin from `x-forwarded-proto` and `x-forwarded-host` when `fromRemoteDevice` is true, and add a route test. The laptop keeps its current path. Then test a chart on a real phone.

**2. REAL PROBLEM (medium): "Only devices signed in to your Tailscale account" is false on a shared tailnet.**
- **Where:** `app/settings/phone-access-card.tsx:25`, `proxy.ts:11-27`.
- **Failure:** on a work or family tailnet, any member whose ACLs allow it who opens the address is signed in automatically and gets the full finance app, including trades and Disconnect. The README warns about this, but the card does not, and the card is what people read.
- **Fix:** at minimum, correct the card copy. Better, have `proxy.ts` compare the `Tailscale-User-Login` header that Serve adds with the laptop owner's login, and refuse anyone else. I confirmed the Funnel header string is in `tailscaled.exe`. The `Tailscale-User-Login` behaviour is from my knowledge of Tailscale, not tested.

**3. REAL PROBLEM (medium): the Funnel guard misses the workflow endpoints, and the card ignores Funnel.**
- **Where:** `proxy.ts:30` (matcher), `lib/phone-access.ts:20-24`.
- **Gap:** `.well-known/workflow/` skips the proxy, so the 403 never runs there. The local-world queue handler (`world-local/dist/queue.js:267`) only checks that its `x-vqs-*` headers parse, with no auth I could find in that handler. With Funnel on, the internet can POST to these routes.
- **Could not verify:** whether this is exploitable, since it likely needs a valid run ID.
- **Other paths are fine:** paths ending in `.png` or similar also skip the proxy, but they skip auto sign-in too, so `requireWorkspace` still returns 401. `_next/static` and `artifact-lib` are public by design.
- **Misleading card:** if the owner enables Funnel, the card still says "On. Only devices signed in…", because `serveSchema` ignores `AllowFunnel`.
- **Fix:** add a matcher entry for `/.well-known/workflow/:path*` with `has: [{ type: "header", key: "tailscale-funnel-request" }]`. Also parse `AllowFunnel` and show a warning on the card.

**4. REAL PROBLEM (medium): after a restart the phone hits a dead end, and the card doesn't warn about it.**
- **Where:** `app/settings/phone-access-card.tsx:25`, `README.md:125`.
- **Failure:** the Tailscale forward persists, but Moneo and Docker don't auto-start (`npm start` is manual). The phone should get a bare proxy error (exact page not checked) with no next step. The card says the computer must be "on and awake" but not that Moneo must be running.
- **README gap:** it gives the Tailscale `--unattended` tip but no restart instructions. It says Moneo must be running, not that `npm start` and Docker are needed again after a restart.
- **Fix:** add a line to the card and the README: "After a restart, start Moneo again on this computer (`npm start`)."

**5. REAL PROBLEM (medium): the card says "off" when Tailscale is merely down.**
- **Where:** `app/settings/phone-access.tsx:7`, `lib/phone-access.ts:53-58`.
- **Failure:** the page turns every state except `on` into `off`. After a restart, or with Tailscale stopped, the forward is still saved but the card shows "Nothing changes unless you turn this on" and a Turn on button. The owner can believe access is off, and it comes back when Tailscale reconnects.
- **Side effects:** a `Stopped` backend is treated as `signed_out`, so pressing the button runs `tailscale login` and the copy says "sign in" when the user only needs to connect. I did not run `login`, so its effect on a stopped node is unverified. Turn off is also a silent no-op in this state.
- **Fix:** add a distinct "Tailscale isn't connected" state, shown only if a forward can be read or the owner has asked. Use `tailscale up`-style wording for `Stopped` rather than sign-in.

Moneo · open-source personal finance · deep dive

Phone access

How a phone or tablet becomes another screen on the Moneo running on your computer, without putting your money on the internet.

Tailscale ServeWireGuardNext.js 16HTTPSAdd to Home Screen
Laptop · runs Moneo

Net worth

€ 24,180
Phone

Net worth

€ 24,180

Same data, same screen

Illustrative numbers

The idea

One Moneo. More screens.

Nothing runs on the phone. It shows the Moneo on your computer, so there is nothing to copy, sync or sign in to again.

Laptop browser

localhost:3000

Exactly as it always was.

Phone

Home-screen icon

Opens your private address.

Tablet

Home-screen icon

Same address, and it can rotate.

Your computer

Moneo

Every page, question and sync runs here. A phone sends the same request a laptop tab would, and gets the same answer.

On your computer

Your database

Postgres in Docker, never copied anywhere.

Already signed in

ChatGPT or API key

The phone uses the computer's sign-in.

Already connected

Banks and Scalable

Sync runs on the computer, from any screen.

The route

Moneo never opens a door

It still listens only on 127.0.0.1. Tailscale is the one thing that accepts the connection, and only from your own devices.

Phone

Your address

The browser or home-screen icon opens https://your-pc .your-tailnet .ts.net.

→
Tailscale app

Encrypted tunnel

A WireGuard tunnel from the phone to the computer, from any network.

→
Tailscale Serve

HTTPS on your computer

Ends HTTPS there and forwards to Moneo, keeping the address the phone asked for.

→
Moneo

127.0.0.1:3000

Handles the request like any other. Its session cookie belongs to that device.

→
Docker

127.0.0.1:54321

Only Moneo's server talks to the database and file storage.

Works anywhere

No router changes

Home Wi-Fi or mobile data. No ports forwarded, no public address.

Real HTTPS

The microphone is allowed

Browsers only allow voice calls on secure pages, and installing to the home screen works best there too.

Streaming

Replies still arrive live

Measured through Serve: each line of a test stream arrived within a few milliseconds.

The one command behind all of it: tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:3000

Turning it on

One button that finds the next step

Settings → Keys and connections → Phone and tablet. Each press asks Tailscale where things stand and shows only what is missing.

Default

Off

One line and a Turn on button. Tailscale isn't needed, and nothing else appears.

→
If needed

Install Tailscale

A download link, then Check again.

→
If needed

Sign in

A sign-in link from Tailscale itself.

→
Once ever

Allow secure addresses

Tailscale's approval page for HTTPS on your devices.

→
On

Scan the code

Your address as a QR code, with the three phone steps beside it.

On the phone or tablet

  • Install Tailscale and sign in with the same account
  • Scan the code in Settings
  • Choose Add to Home Screen

Moneo keeps no copy of this setting

  • Tailscale remembers it, and Settings reads it live
  • Turn off removes only Moneo's forward
  • If another app already uses that address, Moneo says so and leaves it alone

In use

You ask on the phone. The laptop does the work.

Your sign-in lives on the computer, so nothing about your AI plan, bank or broker is ever on the phone.

Step 1Phone
You ask “How much did I spend on food this month?”
Step 2Tunnel
The message travels through Tailscale to Moneo on your computer.
Step 3Moneo
Moneo reads your own records and calls the AI with the ChatGPT sign-in or API key saved on the computer.
Step 4Phone
The reply streams back. If the phone locks, the computer finishes the reply and saves it.
EverywhereDatabase
Edits, accepted cards and syncs land in the same database, so every screen has them. Pressing Sync on the phone runs the sync on the computer.
Not a live mirror yet. A chat streams to the screen that asked. Another open screen shows it after reopening or refreshing the chat, and other open pages can take up to 30 seconds. Tracked in issue #166.

The three sign-ins

Connected once, on the computer

Each service sends the browser back to one fixed address on the computer. The laptop's addresses didn't change, so none of these flows did.

ServiceReturns toFrom the phone
Sign in with ChatGPThttp://127.0.0.1:3000/…Chat works with the computer's sign-in. OpenAI only allows that loopback address, so a new sign-in starts on the computer.
Enable Bankinghttps://localhost:3443/…Data and Sync work. A bank login returns to the computer, so connecting or reconnecting starts there.
Scalable Capitalhttp://localhost:3000/…Data and Sync work. Scalable rejected a *.ts.net address when tested, so connecting starts on the computer.
Without a guard

A dead page and a half-made connection

The phone would try to return to its own localhost, which has no Moneo on it.

With the guard

A clear message, and nothing started

Moneo recognizes a *.ts.net request and says to open Moneo on the computer for that one step.

Who can get in

No password, so the network has to be the lock

Moneo signs its one owner in automatically. That is only safe if nobody else can reach it.

Layer 1

Your devices only

Serve answers devices on your Tailscale network. There is no public address to find or attack.

Layer 2

Public traffic refused

If Tailscale Funnel is ever turned on, it marks each request. Moneo's proxy refuses those before the automatic sign-in.

Layer 3

Local services stay local

Moneo, the database and storage still bind to 127.0.0.1. Other devices on your Wi-Fi can't open them.

What Tailscale can and can't see

  • The tunnel is encrypted between your own devices
  • HTTPS ends on your computer, not on a server in between
  • The address appears in public certificate logs; no data does

What this leaves to you

  • Everyone on your Tailscale network gets straight in, so don't add other people
  • A lost phone has access until you remove it in Tailscale
  • Keep a screen lock on your devices

If you never turn it on

Nothing else changes

The feature had to be invisible to anyone who only uses Moneo on their computer.

Added for everyone

Small and measured

  • One card in Settings, loaded separately so it can't hold up the page
  • A Tailscale status check on Settings only: about 100 ms when installed
  • One header check per request in the proxy
Not added

Nothing running in the background

  • No Tailscale requirement
  • No background jobs, new ports or database changes
  • No new code in the browser for the QR code; it's drawn on the server
Fixed along the way

Chat attachments go through Moneo

They used to open from storage on 127.0.0.1, which only exists on the computer. Now they're served by the app, on every device.

Fixed along the way

The installed app can rotate

The portrait lock is gone, so a tablet can use Moneo in landscape.

Decisions

What I chose, and why

ChoseInstead ofBecause
Private TailscaleA public link with a passwordA two-minute install beats putting a finance app's login page on the internet
TailscaleSame Wi-Fi onlyWorks from anywhere, with HTTPS for voice, and other people on the Wi-Fi can't get in
Run it on your computerA cloud serverYour financial data stays on your machine
Tailscale holds the settingA saved setting in MoneoOne source of truth, so Settings can't disagree with what's really running
Start logins on the computerPasting a return address on the phoneYou connect once, and a clumsy copy-and-paste isn't worth it for something so rare
Keep the laptop's addressesMove Moneo to the new addressExisting ChatGPT, bank and Scalable connections keep working untouched

Takeaway

Your phone is another screen.
Your computer stays the app.

Only if you want it

Off by default, one button to turn on or off.

Private by design

Your own devices only, with no public address.

Keep the computer on

It must be awake with Moneo running. Auto-start is issue #165.

- **Where:** `proxy.ts:30` (matcher), `lib/phone-access.ts:20-24`.
- **Gap:** `.well-known/workflow/` skips the proxy, so the 403 never runs there. The local-world queue handler (`world-local/dist/queue.js:267`) only checks that its `x-vqs-*` headers parse, with no auth I could find in that handler. With Funnel on, the internet can POST to these routes.
- **Could not verify:** whether this is exploitable, since it likely needs a valid run ID.
- **Other paths are fine:** paths ending in `.png` or similar also skip the proxy, but they skip auto sign-in too, so `requireWorkspace` still returns 401. `_next/static` and `artifact-lib` are public by design.
- **Misleading card:** if the owner enables Funnel, the card still says "On. Only devices signed in…", because `serveSchema` ignores `AllowFunnel`.

**5. REAL PROBLEM (medium): the card says "off" when Tailscale is merely down.**
- **Where:** `app/settings/phone-access.tsx:7`, `lib/phone-access.ts:53-58`.
- **Failure:** the page turns every state except `on` into `off`. After a restart, or with Tailscale stopped, the forward is still saved but the card shows "Nothing changes unless you turn this on" and a Turn on button. The owner can believe access is off, and it comes back when Tailscale reconnects.
- **Side effects:** a `Stopped` backend is treated as `signed_out`, so pressing the button runs `tailscale login` and the copy says "sign in" when the user only needs to connect. I did not run `login`, so its effect on a stopped node is unverified. Turn off is also a silent no-op in this state.

content.text:
**Phone access is merged to `main` (`ff23a832`) and pushed.** The reviewer found real problems, so I fixed those first. All unit tests (1412 passed, 10 skipped), lint and build pass.

## What the review found and I fixed
| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Charts in AI pages failed on the phone** because the chart library was looked up on the phone itself | Pages now use the address the phone connected to; I confirmed the library loads through your real `ts.net` address |
| **The card wrongly said only your account could get in** | It now says every device on your Tailscale network can, and warns against shared networks |
| **Moneo's background job routes weren't covered by the public traffic block** | They now refuse it too |
| **The card said "off" when Tailscale was only disconnected** | It now says Tailscale isn't connected, and that phone access comes back once it reconnects |
| **Nothing said Moneo must be restarted after a reboot** | Added to the card and `README.md` |
| **Status check could be cut off early**, misreading Tailscale's state | Moneo now reads the status to the end |
| **"Another app" message could be wrong and left you stuck** | It now gives the command to clear it |
| **Tailscale errors were hidden** | The card now shows Tailscale's own reason |

The reviewer also couldn't confirm turning off from the phone itself. I tested it through the real address, and it works without an error page.

**Left as is:**
- The card won't warn you if you turn on Funnel by hand, but Moneo still refuses that traffic.
- Some small wording suggestions.
- I didn't add a permanent browser test, because this flow needs a real Tailscale. My checks were one-off runs, plus unit tests.
- I didn't send the fixes back through a second review.

## The explainer
I added `C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-ebb24ccb\docs\phone-access-deep-dive.html`, also on `main` as `docs/phone-access-deep-dive.html`. It's 10 pages in the same style as the artifacts one: the idea, the route, the switch, a question from the phone, the three sign-ins, security, non-users, decisions and the takeaway. I checked every page fits in light and dark. I didn't make a video script, since you only asked for the HTML.

## Try it on your phone
Your main copy at `C:\codebases\Moneo` is on `t3/artifact-video-and-card-preview`, so switch it to `main` first. I didn't change that checkout.

1. **Update and start Moneo on the laptop:**
   ```sh
   cd C:\codebases\Moneo
   git checkout main
   git pull
   npm ci
   npm run setup
   npm run build
   npm start
   ```
2. **Turn it on:** in Moneo at `http://localhost:3000`, go to **Settings → Keys and connections → Phone and tablet** and press **Turn on**. Your approval from earlier should still apply, so it should go straight to the QR code.
3. **On your phone:** with Tailscale connected on the same account, scan the code and choose **Add to Home Screen**.

Please try these on the real phone, since I couldn't test them here:
- A real chat reply.
- A voice call.
- Locking the phone mid-chat.
- The home-screen install.

### Easiest: let an AI agent install it

If you use an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, it can do the install for you with the `moneo-setup` skill that comes with Moneo. Open the agent in an empty folder and paste:

> Clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo, then set it up by following .agents/skills/moneo-setup/SKILL.md in that repository.

If you already downloaded Moneo, open the agent in the Moneo folder and say **"set up Moneo"**. The agent runs the commands, tells you what each step does, and asks you only for what it can't do itsel

- **Start Moneo:** `npm start` in the Moneo folder (Docker Desktop must be running).
- **Stop Moneo:** press `Ctrl+C`. The database keeps running in Docker; `docker compose stop` stops it.
- **Update Moneo:**
  ```sh
  git pull
  npm ci
  npm run setup
  npm run build
  npm start
  ```
  Your data and secrets are kept.

1	---
2	name: moneo-setup
3	description: Install, set up, start, update or troubleshoot Moneo on the user's own computer. Use when someone says "set up Moneo", "install Moneo", "Moneo won't start", or asks how to add their AI key, bank or Scalable Capital.
4	---
5	
6	# Set up Moneo
7	
8	You are helping a person, often not a developer, run Moneo on their own computer. Do the commands yourself, explain each step in one plain sentence, and only ask them for things you can't do yourself. The README's **Install** section is the same flow written for people.

file.content:
---
name: moneo-setup
description: Install, set up, start, update or troubleshoot Moneo on the user's own computer. Use when someone says "set up Moneo", "install Moneo", "Moneo won't start", or asks how to add their AI key, bank or Scalable Capital.
---

# Set up Moneo

You are helping a person, often not a developer, run Moneo on their own computer. Do the commands yourself, explain each step in one plain sentence, and only ask them for things you can't do yourself. The README's **Install** section is the same flow written for people.

**If you can control a browser or the computer** (browser use, computer use or similar), ask the person once whether you may, then do the clicking yourself: install Git, Node or Docker Desktop, start Docker, open Moneo, go to Settings → Keys and connections, open the Enable Banking control panel. Stop and hand over whenever a password, API key, private key, 2FA code or bank approval is needed: the person types those. Without that control, tell them exactly what to click.

## Rules

- Never ask the person to paste API keys, bank keys or passwords into this chat. Keys go into Moneo's own page: **Settings → Keys and connections**.
- Never edit `.env` by hand, except `API_PORT` / `DB_PORT` for a port clash. `npm run setup` writes everything else.
- Never change `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`, never delete `.env`, and never run `docker compose down -v` or delete the `moneo_*` Docker volumes. That is the person's financial data.
- Only stop processes you started.

## Steps

1. **Check the tools.** Run `git --version`, `node --version` (needs 22 or newer) and `docker info`.
   - Missing Git, Node or Docker: give the download link (git-scm.com/downloads, nodejs.org, docs.docker.com/get-docker) and wait for them to install it.
   - `docker info` fails: Docker Desktop is not running. Ask them to start it and wait until it says it is running.
2. **Get the code.** If you are not already in a Moneo checkout (`package.json` with `"name": "moneo"`), run `git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git` and `cd Moneo`. Then `npm ci`.
3. **Run the setup:** `npm run setup`. It creates `.env` with fresh secrets, starts the database in Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner and makes a local HTTPS certificate. The first run downloads a few GB (about 4 GB of disk). On Windows, tell them a "Security Warning" about installing a certificate may appear and to click **Yes**. It is safe to rerun.
4. **Start Moneo:** `npm run build`, then `npm start` (keep it running; use a background terminal if you can). Open http://localhost:3000.
5. **Turn on the AI.** Ask them to open **Settings → Keys and connections → AI access** and either click **Sign in with ChatGPT** (Go, Plus or Pro plan) or paste an OpenAI API key from https://platform.openai.com/api-keys and click **Save key**. Voice calls need the API key.
6. **Optional: bank.** Follow the README section "Connect your bank". The person creates an Enable Banking application (Production) with redirect URL `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback`, links their own accounts there, and pastes the App ID and `.pem` key into **Settings → Keys and connections → Connected banks**.
7. **Optional: Scalable Capital.** They turn on Agentic Investing in Scalable (Profile → Security), then click **Connect Scalable Capital** in the same Settings section.
8. **Finish** by telling them how to start Moneo next time (`npm start` with Docker running) and how to update (`git pull`, `npm ci`, `npm run setup`, `npm run build`, `npm start`).

## When something goes wrong

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `docker` not found, or "cannot connect to the Docker daemon" | Install or start Docker Desktop, then rerun `npm run setup`. |
| "port is already allocated" for 54321 or 54322 | Add `API_PORT=55421` and `DB_PORT=55422` (any free ports) to `.env` and rerun `npm run setup`. |
| Port 3000 or 3443 in use | Another program (often an older Moneo) runs there. Find it by port, ask before stopping it, then start Moneo again. |
| ".env points at a hosted Supabase" | That `.env` belongs to another setup. Rename it (don't delete it) and rerun `npm run setup`. |
| "Could not create the local HTTPS certificate" | Only bank connections need it. Rerun `npm run setup` and accept the certificate prompt. |
| Chat says "No AI is set up yet" | Step 5. |
| Bank says the return address was rejected | Add `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` as a redirect URL in the Enable Banking application. |
| The page shows a database error after `git pull` | Run `npm run setup` (applies new migrations), then `npm run build` and `npm start`. |

"""Reports, without printing any secret, whether a PEM-like body sits in the pushed checkpoint transcripts."""
import re, subprocess

REFS = ["K7/01M6XCYG9B3E9KK356M5SZZYK7", "HM/01M6XCP3BBQAX39W74MS6950HM", "V6/01M6XBJFKTR1QGXR5951VQTHV6", "1D/01M6XANPBEGCPZNCEE4PCKY81D"]
BODY = re.compile(r"(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{64}(?:\\\\n|\\n|\s)+){3,}")
ENVDUMP = "ENABLE_BANKING_PRIVATE_KEY="

for ref in REFS:
    name = f"refs/entire/checkpoints/{ref}"
    files = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", name], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
    for path in files:
        if not path.endswith((".jsonl", ".txt")):
            continue
        text = subprocess.run(["git", "cat-file", "blob", f"{name}:{path}"], capture_output=True).stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
        at = text.find(ENVDUMP + "\\n") if ENVDUMP + "\\n" in text else text.find(ENVDUMP)
        after = text[at:at + 400] if at >= 0 else ""
        print(ref[:2], path, "size", len(text), "pem-bodies", len(BODY.findall(text)), "END-marker", text.count("END PRIVATE KEY"),
              "REDACTED", text.count("REDACTED"), "| after env name:", re.sub(r"[A-Za-z0-9+/]{12,}", "<b64>", after[:110]).replace("\n", " "))

def sub(p, a, b):
    s = open(p, encoding='utf-8', newline='').read()
    nl = '\r\n' if '\r\n' in s else '\n'
    a, b = a.replace('\n', nl), b.replace('\n', nl)
    assert a in s, (p, a)
    open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='').write(s.replace(a, b, 1))

STEP = """8. **Optional: phone and tablet.** Offer this once and skip it unless they want it. It lets their own phone and tablet use the Moneo on this computer, through their own free Tailscale account.
   - Ask them to open **Settings → Keys and connections → Phone and tablet** and click **Turn on**. The card shows only the step that is missing: install [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/download), sign in, or allow secure addresses. They click **Check again** after each one. The sign-in and approval are theirs to do.
   - The address and QR code come from their own Tailscale. Read them from the card; never type or guess an address.
   - On each phone or tablet: install Tailscale, sign in with the same account, scan the code, then Add to Home Screen.
   - Tell them plainly: everyone on their Tailscale network gets in without a password, so don't use a shared network; never turn on Tailscale Funnel; the computer must stay awake with Moneo running; new ChatGPT, bank and Scalable logins start on the computer.
9. **Finish**"""
ROWS = """| The phone can't open Moneo | Check Tailscale is connected on both devices, the computer is awake, and Moneo and Docker are running (after a restart, `npm start` again). |
| Phone and tablet card says something else is using the address | Often an older Moneo on another port, or another app. Ask whose it is; if it's safe to clear, run `tailscale serve --https=443 off`, then **Check again**. |
| Phone and tablet card says "Access denied" (Linux) | Run `sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER`, then **Check again**. |
| A phone says a login must start on the computer | Expected. Open Moneo on the computer running it to connect; everything else works on the phone. |
| The page shows a database error"""

for path in ['.agents/skills/moneo-setup/SKILL.md', '.claude/skills/moneo-setup/SKILL.md']:
    sub(path, 'or asks how to add their AI key, bank or Scalable Capital.', 'or asks how to add their AI key, bank or Scalable Capital, or use Moneo on their phone or tablet.')
    sub(path, '8. **Finish**', STEP)
    sub(path, '| The page shows a database error', ROWS)

sub('README.md', '- connect your bank or Scalable Capital (optional, see below).\n\nThat\'s it.',
    '- connect your bank or Scalable Capital (optional, see below).\n\nThat\'s it. Want it on your phone or tablet too? See [Use it from your phone or tablet](#use-it-from-your-phone-or-tablet-optional).')
sub('README.md', 'Only devices in your Tailscale account can reach Moneo, and they get in without a password, so don\'t add other people to it.',
    'The address and code are your own, from your own Tailscale account. Only devices on your Tailscale network can reach Moneo, and they get in without a password, so don\'t use a network you share with other people.')
sub('README.md', 'New ChatGPT, bank and Scalable logins start on this computer, because those services only return to its address.',
    'New ChatGPT, bank and Scalable logins start on this computer, because those services only return to its address. On Linux, first run `sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER`.\n\nHow it works, step by step: [docs/phone-access-deep-dive.html](docs/phone-access-deep-dive.html).')
sub('scripts/setup.mjs', '     Connecting a bank or Scalable Capital is optional and is done there too.\n',
    '     Connecting a bank or Scalable Capital is optional and is done there too.\n     So is using Moneo from your phone or tablet (Phone and tablet).\n')
sub('lib/ai/app-guide.ts', 'Phone and tablet (optional private access through Tailscale; new ChatGPT, bank and Scalable logins still start on the computer)',
    "Phone and tablet (optional private access through the owner's own Tailscale account: press Turn on, then scan the code the card shows; new ChatGPT, bank and Scalable logins still start on the computer)")
